tasks.title: Document the mai-code-2 evidence
tasks.goal: Add the D6 evidence section before any README link points to it. The section must turn B40 through B44 telemetry into a traceable account without overstating qualification.

references.why: D6 extends the design note that records each Copilot model's evidence and qualification status
D6 must preserve the B40 HTTP 503 halt's exit code and uncounted-attempt detail

acceptance: The design note has the exact heading "## mai-code-2 in the loop (2026-11)" and records the URL shortener run as 10 of 10 tasks, 10 first-pass, about $1.31, explicitly measured in an acceptance repository outside this repository.
The section names B40 through B44 with task count, first-pass count and cost.total_usd rounded to cents exactly as read from each committed metrics snapshot, including B42's halted attempt.

The section names every session kind B40 through B44 ran, says no second review ran, and records that B40 through B45 brief reviews ran on mai-code-2 with their kept records under .vloop/state/brief-reviews/.

The section records B39's $8.10 Claude comparison from its run record, B40's HTTP 503 exit 7 with no attempt counted, real defects caught by reviews and gate disputes, and operator-found defects in B42 and B43.
No claim says or implies that mai-code-2 is qualified under the evaluation rule.

references.why: D1 and D3 revise the opening, prerequisites, quickstart, loop summary, operator prompt and Copilot evidence sentence
The unchanged model-qualification rule prevents the mai-code-2 run evidence from being described as qualification
D3's README sentence must link the model evidence section added by T1

acceptance: README.md's opening names both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI, says an agent plans the brief, and no longer contains "vloop has Claude plan it".

Prerequisites names the copilot CLI and a usable GitHub login when Copilot runs, while retaining the two Claude-specific bullets; quickstart says doctor checks the agent CLIs in use rather than Claude alone.
The loop summary says a fresh agent session for Claude Code or Copilot CLI, and "You ask; the skill drives" addresses the user's agent rather than Claude Code alone.

The Copilot section adds the prescribed mai-code-2 sentence for the URL shortener and B40 through B44, links D6's section, names every session kind but the second review, and says it is not yet qualified.
Neither "Every session is a fresh Claude session" nor "mai-code-2 is qualified" appears, and the gpt-6.1-terra sentence still limits plan and gate review to Claude and leaves verify untried.

tasks.title: Explain mixed teams in the README
tasks.goal: Apply D2 to README.md after its agent-neutral edits. The README needs one short mixed-OS entry point plus accurate install and Windows-only Copilot guidance.

references.why: D2 places the mixed-team section, trims the Copilot Windows bullet and updates install guidance
The short README summary must agree with the full mixed-team configuration rules
C-5 constrains mixed-team gates to shared pwsh and forbids local or environment overrides of platforms and shell

acceptance: README.md has a section headed "## Mixed macOS and Windows teams" after Quickstart and before the Copilot section, and its body is at most 150 words.

That section states the shared platforms and shell values, the refusal of local or environment overrides, the fixed-command portability lint, portable pwsh cmdlets and project toolchain, UTF-8 execution, and that this repository is such a team.

The section links docs/guide/configuration.md#mixed-teams, and the Copilot Windows bullet retains only the PowerShell hook plus the B40 through B44 Copilot-on-Windows evidence and links back to the mixed-team section.
README no longer says Windows is untested; Install points Windows users to the PowerShell PATH line in concepts.md, then explains self-update and the per-repository vloop upgrade step.
No mixed-team claim contradicts docs/guide/configuration.md.

tasks.title: Update the guides for any agent
tasks.goal: Apply D4 consistently across the four guides. Agent-neutral prose must describe only where Claude and Copilot genuinely share behavior, while preserving agent-specific mechanisms.

references.why: D4 revises fresh sessions, repository guidelines, interactive plugin loading, eval replay and mixed-team gate guidance
D4 adds the Copilot token, cost, credit and cache-hit-ratio rules
D4 changes each model.* value to distinguish Claude aliases from Copilot model ids
D4 distinguishes claude plugin eval from agent-eval without changing the qualification rule
S-1 requires fresh processes for either agent, P-5 makes the plan shell govern gates, and C-5 defines mixed-team portability
It is the source for how Claude sessions receive repository guidelines through the appended system-prompt file
It is the source for Copilot custom instructions and credit-based estimated cost with no token report

acceptance: concepts.md says each configured agent runs a fresh agent session, explains both guideline delivery mechanisms, shows both interactive plugin-dir commands, names agent-eval for other agents, and adds a short mixed-team portable-gates note.
metrics.md says Copilot reports no tokens, estimates cost from copilot.credit-usd with cost_source estimated, sums every phase in credits.total, and counts cache_hit_ratio for Claude sessions only.
All seven model.* values explain that the setting is a Claude alias or model name, or a Copilot model id when that phase's agent is copilot; the old "any model name" value is absent.
evals.md's Calls claude row says claude plugin eval calls claude and tools/agent-eval calls the agent it is given, while the qualification rule remains unchanged.
No Claude-specific adapter, installation or qualification wording is made generic, and all new statements agree with the driver implementation.
